name: Philippines
genZNote: The Philippines is 7,600+ islands strong and spent over 300 years under Spain followed by decades under the US — which is exactly why it's the only major Asian nation that's both majority Catholic AND has English as an official, widely spoken language.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: An archipelago of over 7,600 islands in Southeast Asia, grouped into three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Located on the Pacific Ring of Fire, making it highly prone to typhoons, earthquakes, and volcanic activity.
Tropical maritime climate, with the capital Manila located on the largest island, Luzon.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Filipino (based on Tagalog) and English are both official languages, a legacy of Spanish and later American colonial rule.
The only majority Roman Catholic nation in Asia, a lasting legacy of over three centuries of Spanish colonisation.
Known for strong family-centred social values, vibrant fiesta traditions, and globally influential overseas Filipino worker (OFW) communities.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic modelled closely on the US system, with a President as head of state and government and a bicameral Congress.
Ruled by Spain for over 300 years, then by the United States from 1898, before gaining full independence in 1946.
The 1986 'People Power Revolution' peacefully ended the Marcos dictatorship and restored democratic governance.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A major global source of skilled healthcare professionals, particularly nurses, who work extensively abroad while supporting a growing domestic healthcare sector.
Active in disaster-resilience science and engineering given its high exposure to typhoons and earthquakes.
Growing business process outsourcing (BPO) and IT services sector, leveraging widespread English proficiency.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding ASEAN member and a treaty ally of the United States, with close historical and defence ties.
Involved in ongoing South China Sea territorial disputes with China, particularly around the West Philippine Sea.
A major source of global remittance income through its large overseas worker population.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and the Philippines maintain warm, growing relations, with cooperation expanding in defence (including the BrahMos missile deal, a landmark Indian defence export), trade, and IT services.
Both countries share strong English-language business process outsourcing industries, creating some economic parallels and cooperation potential.
Part of India's outreach under the Act East policy and growing Indo-Pacific security cooperation.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A services-driven economy strong in business process outsourcing (BPO), electronics assembly, and remittances from overseas Filipino workers.
Major exporter of electronics components, coconut products, and agricultural goods.
Remittances from overseas workers form one of the largest shares of GDP among major economies globally.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being Asia's only majority Roman Catholic nation.
A globally significant overseas workforce and remittance economy.
World-class beaches and biodiversity, including the Tubbataha Reefs.
The 1986 People Power Revolution as a landmark peaceful pro-democracy movement.
A major recent defence customer for India's BrahMos missile system.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Philippine Peso (PHP).
A services-driven economy, globally significant in business-process outsourcing (BPO) and call centres; remittances from overseas Filipino workers are a major income source.
Agriculture (notably rice and coconut) remains important, especially in rural areas.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: An archipelago of over 7,000 islands with exceptional marine biodiversity, part of the 'Coral Triangle'.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a UNESCO World Heritage marine protected area.
Highly vulnerable to typhoons and volcanic activity, given its location on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Colonized by Spain for over 300 years, then ceded to the United States after the 1898 Spanish-American War.
Gained independence from the US in 1946 after Japanese occupation during World War II.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1946 independence from the United States.
The 1986 'People Power Revolution' peacefully ended the Marcos dictatorship; the 1987 Constitution restored democratic governance.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Basketball is the most popular sport nationwide, a legacy of American influence.
The Banaue Rice Terraces are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, built by hand over 2,000 years ago.
A globally significant source of seafarers, staffing a large share of the world's merchant shipping crews.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of ASEAN.
Member of the UN; maintains a long-standing mutual defence treaty with the United States.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Philippines is a Southeast Asian archipelagic presidential republic, Asia's only majority Catholic nation, with deep historical Spanish and American colonial influence.
keyFacts: Presidential republic modelled on the US system.
Independent from the US in 1946, after over 300 years of Spanish rule.
Asia's only majority Roman Catholic country.
commonConfusion: The Philippines' two official languages are Filipino and English — Spanish, though historically dominant, is not a current official language.

highYieldFacts: Philippines: presidential republic, capital Manila, independent from the US in 1946.
Asia's only majority Catholic nation, due to over 300 years of Spanish rule.
India-Philippines: BrahMos missile deal is a landmark Indian defence export.
commonTraps: Assuming Spanish is still an official language — it is not; Filipino and English are.
Confusing the Philippines' South China Sea dispute area (West Philippine Sea) terminology with China's claims.
mustRemember: Philippines: Catholic-majority, US-modelled presidential republic, major BPO/remittance economy, BrahMos missile customer.
